1004476.etyen:
Alteration of fanden (“the Devil; damn”), under the influence of fark (“vagrant, rogue”).
The former is from Old Norse fendinn (“the Devil”), probably from Old Frisian fandiand (“tempter”), the present participle of fandia (“to tempt”), from *fandōną (“to seek, search for, examine”), ultimately from the Proto-Indo-European root *pent- (“to pass; path”). Because this branch beyond Old Norse is probable rather than certain, it is not used for categorical derivation here.

1004732.etyen:
From Mathias (“male given name”) + -sen (“patronymic suffix meaning “son of””), originally a patronymic meaning “son of Mathias”. It later became established as a hereditary surname.
Compare the parallel formations Danish Mathiassen and Mathiasen, and Swedish Mathiasson (“patronymic surname”).

1004988.etyen:
Partial calque of English spot rate. Compound of spot (“spot; for immediate delivery”) + kurs (“rate, exchange rate”), literally “spot rate”.
The first element, spot (“spot; for immediate delivery”), is borrowed from English spot (“spot; for immediate delivery”).
The final element, kurs (“rate, exchange rate”), is through French cours (“course; rate”) from Latin cursus (“course, run”), from currō (“to run”), ultimately from the Proto-Indo-European root *ḱers- (“to run”).
Compare the parallel formations Norwegian Nynorsk spotkurs, Danish spotkurs and Swedish spotkurs (“spot rate”).
